speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy with feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To understand what is causing your discomfort, can you tell me when these symptoms first started and if you have noticed any vomiting or blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception. The clinical presentation of an 8-month-old with abdominal distension, feeding difficulties, and severe pain (crying on palpation) is highly suggestive of intussusception, a surgical emergency requiring immediate confirmation via ultrasound.
